subject: Pricing & commit tiers: marketplace vs direct billing impact
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & commit tiers: marketplace vs direct billing impact

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on the usage patterns you shared (peaks for inference-heavy analytics and a baseline of ~8–12M tokens/month), I put together an initial pricing grid and a draft SOW attached. Two quick questions up front so we can land a final commercial path:

1) Do you expect to procure via AWS Marketplace (Company account) or through a direct Redwood invoice?
2) If marketplace, will Acme require that the committed discount be reflected on the marketplace invoice (vs. us issuing a credit)?

High-level proposal (draft):
- Commit tier 1: 1–10M tokens / month -> $0.018 per 1k tokens (net)
- Commit tier 2: 10–50M tokens / month -> $0.012 per 1k tokens (net)
- Term: 12 months with quarterly usage reviews and a 30-day roll-out window

If you go direct, we can lock the net per-token rates above. If you go through Marketplace, there is typically a channel fee that affects the gross invoice — we can either adjust listing price or use a private offer to preserve the effective net price, but I want to confirm how your procurement team prefers to see it.

I attached a pricing-grid.xlsx and a short SOW for review. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm the path so I can get legal and finance lined up?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: pricing-grid.xlsx (Excel), SOW-draft.pdf (PDF)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the files. A couple of clarifying points from Acme procurement:

- We plan to route purchases through our AWS consolidated billing (Marketplace) to keep vendor billing centralized.
- We need the committed discount to appear on the invoice we pay via Marketplace, or else we need a formal credit note process tied to our PO — procurement strongly prefers the discount on the Marketplace invoice.
- We expect roughly 10M tokens/mo to start, ramping to 30M by Q4 if throughput looks good.
- Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to issue a private offer (Marketplace) that reflects the committed/discounted unit price?

If a private offer is an option, we can move faster — procurement just needs confirmation on mechanics and any timing risk for closing the private offer.

Thanks,
Daniel Park

daniel.park@acmerobotics.com

Sean / Karthik —

Looping you both in for quick internal alignment. Acme will route via AWS Marketplace and procurement wants the discount reflected on the marketplace invoice (private offer preferred). Questions we need to confirm before we reply:

- Our standard stance: direct contracts can carry the net commit pricing. For marketplace customers we can do one of: (a) create a Private Offer with adjusted list price to reflect channel fee and still give the customer the same effective net price, or (b) keep list price and issue Redwood-side credits to match net price.
- Rough channel/marketplace fee assumption is ~8–12% (varies by program/region). Do we have a canonical % for quoting?
- Any limits on committing to a multi-month price through Private Offer vs. direct invoice? Finance + Legal need to confirm whether Private Offer locks are treated differently for revenue recognition.

Proposed quick responses: give Acme two paths (direct invoice = simplest, Private Offer via AWS = fine if we can confirm channel fee and timeline). Sean — can you engage AWS contact and confirm whether Private Offer can preserve their requested invoice-level discount? Karthik — can you flag finance/legal if Private Offer terms cause any revenue recognition caveat?

I’ll hold off replying to Acme until we have those answers.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:44 -07:00
Subject: Question: Private Offer & discount pass-through mechanics

Hi —

We have a prospective customer (Acme Robotics) who will likely purchase via AWS Marketplace but requires that negotiated commit discounts appear on the Marketplace invoice. Our typical commercial options are:

1) Direct Redwood invoice with agreed net per-token prices (straightforward).
2) Marketplace Private Offer (custom listing/price) to reflect negotiated unit price on the Marketplace invoice.
3) Marketplace listing at standard price + Redwood-issued post-sale credit to the buyer.

Can you confirm: which of the above is the recommended pattern to ensure (a) the buyer sees the committed discount on their invoice, and (b) the seller (Redwood) can still apply the negotiated net price without unexpected channel margin impact? Also: what is the typical Marketplace transaction fee % that we should bake into the gross listing price if creating a Private Offer? Any links to docs or a short note about timing for Private Offer creation would be great.

Thanks for any help — copying internal folks and the buyer so we can close quickly.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>
Bcc: 
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:37:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: Private Offer & discount pass-through mechanics

Hi Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers:

- Private Offer is the recommended path when a buyer needs to see a negotiated price on their Marketplace invoice. Private Offers allow you to specify a custom unit price (or discount) for a specific buyer and will appear on the AWS Marketplace invoice.
- Transaction fees vary by program and the chosen commerce model (SaaS contract, usage-based metering, AMI, etc.). For usage-based SaaS, a typical transaction fee range is 8–12%, though certain programs/regions may differ. We can confirm the exact % for your Redwood seller account.
- Private Offers can be created quickly once both parties accept — typical turnaround is 3–7 business days for a straightforward offer.

A few practical notes:
- If you want the buyer to see the same "net" price as a direct Redwood invoice, you should set the Private Offer price so that after Marketplace fees the seller effective revenue equals the agreed net. In practice we see sellers either (a) increase list price to cover fees and publish a Private Offer for the net price, or (b) keep list price and coordinate post-sale credits; option (a) is cleaner for procurement because the invoice shows the negotiated price directly.
- We can also route through the AWS Private Marketplace / Private Catalog for enterprise buyers who want internal controls.

Link: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/private-offers.html

If helpful, I can start the Private Offer creation for Acme once Redwood confirms the desired final unit price (gross). Please let me know the Redwood seller account ID and the final gross unit price you want us to list for the offer.

Regards,
Jake Morales
AWS Marketplace Sales
aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com

Subject: Re: Pricing & commit tiers: marketplace vs direct billing impact

Daniel —

Quick summary and two proposed commercial paths so you can pick the one procurement prefers.

Context: AWS confirms Private Offer is supported and shows negotiated pricing on the Marketplace invoice. Marketplace typically takes ~8–12% transaction fee; to preserve Redwood's agreed net price we have two viable approaches:

Path A — Direct Redwood invoice (preferred by finance/legal):
- Redwood bills Acme directly at the net commit pricing in the attached grid.
- Pros: clean revenue recognition, no channel fee, fastest to contract.
- Cons: Acme will not have the usage on the AWS Marketplace invoice (may complicate internal chargeback).

Path B — AWS Marketplace Private Offer (if you need the discount on the Marketplace invoice):
- Redwood creates a Private Offer with a gross unit price that yields the agreed net after AWS fees. Example: if agreed net is $0.012 per 1k tokens and marketplace fee is 10%, we would set gross list price to ~$0.0133 per 1k tokens in the Private Offer.
- Pros: procurement sees discount on Marketplace invoice, aligns with your AWS billing.
- Cons: gross price is higher due to fee; we’ll need to confirm exact fee % with AWS and lock Private Offer terms (3–7 business days typical).

Suggested next steps:
1) Tell us which path you prefer (A or B).
2) If B, confirm Acme’s AWS account ID so we can initiate the Private Offer flow and we'll request the exact fee % from AWS to finalize gross price.
3) If A, we’ll circulate a short MSA + SOW and a 12-month commit schedule for signature.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to close — what works best for you?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
